propositions: A 68-day read-only audit of 2,265 work tickets and 2,349 commits established reproducible measures of ticket mix, lifecycle throughput, planning/completion outcomes, defect signals, commit governance, and code-health trends, segmented by calendar quarters where sample sizes permit.

Plan-review adoption rose from 29.2% to 79.5% across Q2–Q3 with 49.0% first-pass verdict rate and p90=8 attempts; no current bug has detected_by metadata, so true escape rate and detection-stage efficiency cannot be calculated and caused_by links are advisory and noisy.

Completion first-pass verdict was 72.3% overall; Testing-section tickets showed 79.7% first-pass versus 68.6% without, and declared file-impact tickets 74.2% versus 67.6% undeclared; these are observational associations, not causal estimates.

Code-review funnel showed 97.4% first-pass (1,178/1,209 Gerrit changes), but this describes the observed funnel, not reviewer effectiveness; 35 modules near or above 720 LOC and 4.09% duplication identify debt pressure; same-file retouch within 24h was 47.7% of consecutive pairs, a hotspot/coordination proxy.

Source diffs became smaller (median 111.5→95 lines) and test co-change increased from Q2 to partial Q3; ticket/DCO/Change-Id hygiene reached ~100% adoption by August, supporting process maturation but not proven quality improvement.

Six prioritized recommendations target escaped-defect measurement, deterministic preflight checks, completion-failure classification, risk-tiered review, debt management, and maintainership evidence; all material findings remain QUALIFIED by short window, partial Q3, process changes during observation, and metadata quality rather than rejected.
